problem: Social navigation benchmarks focus on proxemics and task efficiency, and crafting specific human-robot interaction scenarios (edge cases, context-specific) in simulation is labor-intensive. Existing tools (SEAN 2.0, HuNavSim, Arena, SocNavBench) offer limited predefined scenarios or little control over scenario content.
motivation: Perceived social competence and contextual appropriateness depend on the robot's task and location, and testing them needs controlled scenarios plus human judgment. Automating scenario creation with LLM commonsense reasoning and code generation makes scenario-based testing scalable.
key_idea: Use VLMs/LLMs with structured prompts over a user-annotated 2D semantic scene graph to turn simple scenario metadata into scenario descriptions, pedestrian/robot paths, and behavior-tree XML that run in HuNavSim/Gazebo.
insight: Structured, context-rich prompts (scene graph, examples, BT node library) plus error handling matter a lot: a naive VLM baseline got 30% guided and 10% unguided success versus 73% and 55% for the full pipeline. Failures come mostly from wrong behavior tree node choice or ordering and from poor trajectories, which interactive re-querying can fix. The persona case study shows that different navigation algorithms are preferred in different social scenarios.
method: Map annotation: users build a 2D semantic scene graph (nodes/edges with semantic types) over the map image, giving spatial and semantic context and a structure for validating paths.

Scenario proposal: an LLM/VLM turns metadata (social context, task, optional rough scenario, location description) into a detailed scenario description, human behaviors and the robot's expected behavior, using handcrafted few-shot examples.

Path generation: a VLM given the scene graph, the annotated map image and examples outputs simultaneous pedestrian and robot paths, group assignments and encounter nodes; discontinuous paths are detected and trigger re-queries, and users can edit via natural language.

Behavior generation: per-pedestrian LLM prompt with the BT node library and syntax examples outputs HuNavSim behavior-tree XML; the authors added gesture and gesture-recognition nodes for human-robot interaction.

Simulation: scene-graph paths are mapped to world-frame goals or waypoints in HuNavSim/ROS2/Gazebo; gestures are integer-coded ROS2 topics; a scenario manager node synchronizes pedestrian timing with the robot's position; any Nav2-based planner can be tested.

setting.observation: user-annotated 2D map image and semantic scene graph plus textual scenario metadata
setting.action_space: not applicable to the generator (it outputs scene-graph paths and behavior trees); the evaluated robots use Nav2 planners (MPPI etc.)
setting.privileged: user-annotated scene graph of the map

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark; results are scenario-generation success rates, cost, time and a user study, not in the canonical benchmark format. Persona-study PSI scores are given only in a figure.
results: The pipeline reached 73% success for guided and 55% for unguided scenario generation, versus 30% and 10% for a naive VLM baseline. It takes about 43 s and under $0.30 per scenario (~15k input tokens with GPT-4o). In the usability study it worked for 4 of 5 researchers, all of whom preferred it to manual creation. In the persona case study (40 Prolific participants per scenario) it cut the estimated effort from about a month to 4 days.
limitations: Manual map annotation is required, and generated trajectories or behaviors can be wrong or mistimed (e.g., the warehouse group scenario needed manual fixes); 27-45% of first-cut scenarios fail.
There is no automatic validation that a generated scenario matches the user's intent, and the small user study (5 researchers) and limited scenarios (4) are only preliminary evidence.
Only one simulator (Gazebo/HuNavSim) is supported, with limited crowd size.
